# Results

Snapshot of 22 October 2026, Ollama v0.40.7. For each model, the text the model would read
was produced three ways (the maker's template, the copy inside the model file, and what Ollama
uses) for six practice conversations that involve tools. A model "differs" if, in at least
one of them, Ollama's text changes what the model is told compared with the maker's. Spaces,
line breaks, the date and the start-of-text marker don't count. [How it works](how-it-works.html)
explains the method.

## Summary

| | Differs | Differs, order-only set aside | Built for tools: differs | Built for tools: order-only set aside |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ollama library | 32 of 43 | 28 of 43 | 15 of 19 | 11 of 19 |
| Hugging Face | 5 of 22 | 5 of 22 | 4 of 21 | 4 of 21 |

"Order-only" means the only change is the order of the fields inside a tool's description,
for example `required` listed before `properties`. "Built for tools" means the maker's own
template shows the model the list of tools.

### Not compared

- `orca-mini:latest`: latest = 3b-q4_0, from pankajmathur/orca_mini_3b. That repo has no chat template; its prompt format is given only as prose in the model card.
- `starcoder2:latest`: latest = 3b-q4_0, the base completion model bigcode/starcoder2-3b, which has no chat template (starcoder2:instruct is a separate, non-default tag).
- `llama2-uncensored:latest`: latest = 7b-chat-q4_0, from georgesung/llama2_7b_chat_uncensored, which has no chat template.
- `mistral-small3.2:latest`: latest = 24b-instruct-2506-q4_K_M. Mistral's repo ships tekken.json, params.json and SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt for mistral-common and no Jinja chat template.
- `minimax-m2.7:cloud`: Cloud-only in Ollama: the tags page lists only `cloud`, so there is no local package (no GGUF, Go template or selection) to audit. The author repo does have chat_template.jinja.
- `gpt-oss:latest`: Ollama lays out this model's conversations with special code ("harmony") that this study doesn't reproduce.
- `translategemma:latest`: The maker's template could not show any of the six tool conversations.

## How often the check-up's template warning fires

The check-up's template rules were run over 95 different templates
from 65 models in this study (the maker's, the model file's and Ollama's). It
flagged 3. Read by hand, each one is a visible feature, not
hidden instructions:

- `gpt-oss:latest` (author): reacts to `<|channel|>analysis<|message|>`, `<|channel|>final<|message|>`.
- `hf.co/peculiar-ragdoll/Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-GGUF-MTP:Q4_K_XL` (gguf): reacts to `<|think_extreme|>`, `<|think_high|>`, `<|think_low|>`, `<|think_max|>`, `<|think_medium|>`, `<|think_minimal|>`, `<|think_off|>`, `<|think_on|>`, `<|think_ultracode|>`, `<|think_xhigh|>`.
- `hf.co/peculiar-ragdoll/Dirk-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M` (gguf): reacts to `<|think_extreme|>`, `<|think_high|>`, `<|think_low|>`, `<|think_max|>`, `<|think_medium|>`, `<|think_minimal|>`, `<|think_off|>`, `<|think_on|>`, `<|think_ultracode|>`, `<|think_xhigh|>`.

The two models with `<|think_…|>` words let you switch their thinking mode by typing those
words. `gpt-oss` uses its channel markers to separate its reasoning from its answer.

## Known gaps

- Mistral's own templates accept only nine-character tool request numbers. The practice
  conversations use `call_1`, so those comparisons couldn't run and aren't counted.
- The automatic sorter doesn't know a few model-specific markers (DeepSeek's start-of-text
  marker, for example), so it labels them "other wording". Each was checked by hand. The
  others are real wording differences. The DeepSeek marker is not, but no model's result
  depends on it.
- A file with no template of its own can't be checked for old copies.
